title: Meet J, K and L
goal: Recognise, name and write J, K, L.
cue: A letter has a name. Later, we will learn the sounds it can represent in words. Today, say the letter names.
spelling: A letter has a name. Later, we will learn the sounds it can represent in words. Today, say the letter names.
task: Point to J and L. Say their names, then write their lowercase partners.
story: The letter J has a big form and a small form.
reviewPrompt: Recall two letters from day 3 before looking back.

cards.title: Letter J
sections: In juice, j represents /dʒ/. This is a word sound, not the letter name.
Write J and j three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

articulation.label: Letter J
articulation.alt: Letter J: /dʒ/ → /eɪ/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /dʒ/: Brief closure and release, with voice.
/ɪ/: Raise the front tongue; narrow the jaw gap.
articulation.note: Keep each vowel glide inside one syllable.

articulation.label: Letter K
articulation.alt: Letter K: /k/ → /eɪ/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.

articulation.label: Letter L
articulation.alt: Letter L: /ɛ/ → /l/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /ɛ/: Front tongue; open the jaw a little more.
/l/: Tip at the ridge; air passes round the sides.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Five words to hear and use
sections: A sweet food made from fruit and sugar. I like jam on bread.
a light object flown in the wind on a string. The kite is high in the sky.
a flat, usually green part of a plant. A green leaf falls from the tree.
a small metal object used to open a lock. Puck looks for his key.
one of the body parts used for standing and walking. His leg is fine.
Listen to each word. Point or act to show its meaning. Say one word, then one short sentence. Ask for help with spelling patterns you have not learned yet.
